key_insight: Molecular flexibility reshapes epitaxial registry by balancing molecule–template interactions against conformational energy while preserving intermolecular bonding networks.
engineering_relevance: Accounting for molecular conformation could improve the design of multilayer molecular architectures with controlled interfaces.
method: Studied intact BTB on a fully deprotonated BTB δ-layer supported by Ag(111).
Combined scanning tunneling microscopy, low-energy electron microscopy and diffraction, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy.
Used density functional theory to compare flexible and planar-constrained adsorption geometries.
evidence_signal: Site-dependent microscopy appearances agree with calculated conformational variations, and planar constraints change the predicted preferred lateral adsorption positions.
watch_item: The abstract establishes the mechanism for BTB on a specific molecular template; its generality across other molecules and interfaces remains to be tested.
paper_title: Conformationally frustrated epitaxy at heteromolecular interface
